html:
The Mozambique floods of 2000 were weeks of flooding in southern Mozambique in February and March 2000, caused by heavy rain and then Cyclone Leon-Eline.

Rain fell for about four weeks over southern Africa. Then the cyclone came ashore and the rivers, above all the Limpopo, burst their banks across the flat coastal plain. Towns such as Chókwè and Xai-Xai went under. About 800 people died, hundreds of thousands lost their homes, and large areas of farmland and herds were ruined.

Images of people stranded on roofs and in trees went around the world. Helicopters from South Africa and other countries plucked survivors to safety. One woman gave birth in a tree before being rescued, and her baby became a symbol of the disaster.

Mozambique was only eight years out of the civil war, and the floods washed away roads and bridges rebuilt since the peace. The water also shifted landmines into new places. Later storms such as Cyclone Idai in 2019 showed how exposed the country's low coast remains.
sum: The Mozambique floods of 2000 were weeks of flooding in southern Mozambique in February and March 2000, caused by heavy rain and then Cyclone Leon-Eline.
